source.title: Fitting Vision Adapters at Frontier Scales
source.authors: Jaehoon Lee; Harry B. Partridge; M. Jayasekara; Charles O'Neill; Max Kirkby; Michael Psenka

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures an affine mapping between token-embedding spaces from different model families. This bears narrowly on interchangeability by a simple map, but it does not measure the original cross-model convergence claim across scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-scale benchmark performance and within-model image/text geometry, but those benchmark scores do not measure cross-model representation alignment. The affine token-embedding fit in Section 3.2 is the result that bears on V4. The image/text centroid measurements and image-token-to-vocabulary cosine are recorded as related findings, not as tests of cross-model convergence.
record.test_reason: Section 3.2 reports one incidental result on V4. An ordinary-least-squares affine map from the Kimi reader's token embeddings to Qwen3 readers' embeddings, over a shared 95k-token vocabulary, leaves validation relative MSE of 0.77–0.89 (cosine 0.36–0.50). The authors call cross-family token geometries 'far from affinely equivalent.' That is a numeric result against a simple linear map with little loss, so it fits T5 better than T2: it is not a method aimed at the convergence question, just a residual reported along the way. Everything else in the paper is adapter benchmarking or within-model geometry.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right. Its framing of the main conclusion is accurate: a ≈50M adapter gives frozen text-only LMs strong visual competence (56.8% MMMU-Pro at 743B). It should add three points. First, gains plateau at frontier scale, with two unrelated frontier readers within 0.1 points. Second, cross-image comparison does not emerge from single-image training. Third, image tokens enter nearly orthogonal to text tokens and merge over depth. The affine-map residual is a side finding: the initialisation gives 'a coarse orientation' and gradient descent does the rest.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not apply the original cross-model representation-similarity method. Its relevant measurement fits an affine map to shared-vocabulary token embeddings and reports the residual.

fits_no_version.finding: In the frozen GLM-5.2 reader, the cosine between the mean image token and the mean text token rises from 0.02 at input to 0.46 at layer 12 and 0.91 at layer 77. A PCA shows the populations remain largely separable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inside one frozen multimodal reader, adapter-injected image tokens and text tokens converge in direction with depth without fully merging.

fits_no_version.finding: The adapter's image-token outputs have mean max-cosine 0.059 to any vocabulary embedding, versus 0.057 for random vectors of the same norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapter outputs that a frozen LM can use need not lie near its word-embedding coordinates.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Grounded and Faithful Vision-Language Models for Real-World Deployment (VLM4RWD)
record.problems: The cross-family affine-map evidence is limited to shared-vocabulary token embeddings and Kimi→Qwen3 pairs; the paper does not establish how those results generalize to other representation levels or model families. The main scale comparisons include models trained with different configurations, and the paper notes that these comparisons do not isolate model size.
record.rows_left_out: Benchmark accuracy, blind-control, corruption, and task-specific training results are omitted because they do not measure representation convergence. Other interpretability results, including probes and steering interventions, do not compare representations across independently trained models.

untested.parts: No alignment between independently trained models is measured as a function of scale. Benchmark accuracy rising with reader size is not a representation-alignment measure.
No alignment of vision and language models on paired image–caption data. The adapter's success is task accuracy after training, not a similarity measure.
No seed comparisons; the authors state that runs are single seed.

Not tested: mapping of hidden-layer representations, non-affine maps, relative representations, unpaired methods, and family pairs other than Kimi→Qwen3. The trained vision→LM adapter is task-optimised stitching, but no mapping-loss measure is reported for it.
No comparison of features or circuits across models.
No variation of the similarity metric or input distribution for cross-model alignment.
No analysis of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: This is a vision-adapter paper, and the V4 bearing rests on a single aggregate sentence. Its scope is narrow: input token embeddings, two model families (the authors note this as a limitation), and no per-pair numbers. Figure 6 says GLM-5.2's affine-initialised SFT loss starts at 0.86, below the Qwen3 plateau. That hints the coarse map carries some usable signal, but it is not a mapping-loss measure. Benchmark gains with reader scale (Qwen3 4B–32B, MoE models) are not representation alignment, and the MoE comparisons use different training configurations. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure representational alignment between independently trained models as size or capability changes.
It does not measure alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as both models improve.
No same-architecture, different-initialization representation comparison is reported.

The mapping result concerns shared-vocabulary token embeddings for Kimi→Qwen3 pairs. It does not test mapping general hidden representations, layer stitching, relative representations, unpaired mappings, or other model families.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models is reported.
The study does not compare cross-model convergence under alternative similarity settings or input distributions.
The study does not test whether shared data or objectives explain cross-model representational alignment.

rows.subject: Kimi→Qwen3 reader pairs (aggregate; exact target models not specified for this result)
rows.operation_detail: Fit an affine map between shared-vocabulary token embeddings by ordinary least squares and measure its validation residual

conditions.value: source reader token embeddings to target reader token embeddings

rows.measure: Validation relative MSE and cosine similarity
rows.note: The paper describes the cross-family token geometries as far from affinely equivalent. The reported result is aggregate across Kimi→Qwen3 pairs.
rows.check: The link to V4 and the state 'absent' are right. Fix the subject to 'source = the vision encoder's original companion reader (Kimi) → target Qwen3 readers (4B–32B), aggregate range'; per-pair values are not given. The baseline is not stated. Note that relative MSE is normalised by the target embedding norms, so a value of 1.0 corresponds to predicting zero, and 0.77–0.89 is only modestly better than trivial. The measure covers input token embeddings only, not hidden representations.

source_check.correct: Source: the vision encoder's original companion reader (Kimi). Targets: Qwen3 readers, whose studied sizes are 4B, 8B, 14B and 32B. Validation relative MSE 0.77–0.89; cosine similarity 0.36–0.50. Results are aggregate; individual pair values are not reported.

rows.subject: GLM-5.2 adapter image-token outputs

relation.reason: The study measures the validation error of an affine map between independently trained readers' token embeddings, directly bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The large validation residuals directly challenge low-loss affine interchangeability for the tested input-embedding pairs.

source_check.notes: The mapping uses a shared vocabulary of 95,369 tokens. The reported ranges have no per-pair breakdown or uncertainty estimates; subsequent projector training does not establish low-loss affine interchangeability.

statements.correction: Qwen3 target sizes: 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B. Kimi source-reader size: not stated. Section 3.2 reports aggregate Kimi→Qwen3 mapping residuals; no corresponding residual is reported for a target above 100B.
statements.problem: The absence of a reported embedding-map result above 100B is consistent with the text, but describing R1's model sizes as entirely unstated overlooks the identified Qwen3 target sizes.
